'''Malcolm Golby Haines''' (12 October 1936 – 13 January 2013)<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Krushelnick|first1=Karl|last2=Dangor|first2=Bucker|last3=VanDevender|first3=Pace|last4=Beg|first4=Farhat|author4-link=Farhat Beg|date=2013|title=Obituary of Malcolm Haines (1936-2013)|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/do/10.1063/PT.4.1725/abs/|journal=Physics Today|language=EN|doi=10.1063/PT.4.1725|url-access=subscription}}</ref> was a British plasma [[physicist]] known for his research on [[Z-pinch]]es.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|title=Professor Malcolm Haines|newspaper=[[The Times]]|language=en|url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/science/article/professor-malcolm-haines-q3dj3qfj7mv|access-date=2020-12-08|issn=0140-0460}}</ref> He was a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1995&unit_id=&institution=Imperial+College+London|access-date=2020-12-08|website=American Physical Society|language=en}}</ref> and was co-awarded the 2005 [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Alfvén Prize {{!}} European Physical Society – Plasma Physics Division|url=http://plasma.ciemat.es/eps/awards/alfven-prize/|access-date=2020-12-08|language=en-US}}</ref> 

== Early life and career ==
Haines studied at [[Imperial College London]] in 1953 and has remained there for the rest of his life. He obtained a [[Bachelor of Science]] (B.S.) and [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (Ph.D.) in 1957 and 1960 respectively. He then joined the Imperial College faculty as a lecturer in 1960, was promoted to senior lecturer in 1967 and later appointed Professor of Physics. He retired in 2002, but was still active in research in the Plasma Physics Group as [[emeritus professor]].<ref name=":3" />

== Scientific contributions ==
After Russian scientists led by [[Valentin Panteleimonovich Smirnov|Valentin Smirnov]] had achieved a breakthrough in plasma physics by using rod grids in [[Z-pinch]] arrangements, Haines optimized the grids and other experimental parameters and undertook theoretical simulations of the [[Implosion (mechanical process)|implosion]] processes. They were tested on MAGPIE (Mega Ampere Generator for Plasma Implosion Experiments) at Imperial College.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2006-10-14|title=Magpie Project Home Page|url=http://dorland.pp.ph.ic.ac.uk/magpie/experiments/index.html|access-date=2020-12-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061014233406/http://dorland.pp.ph.ic.ac.uk/magpie/experiments/index.html|archive-date=14 October 2006}}</ref> The method revolutionized the research of [[inertial fusion]] with Z-pinch arrangements (and their use as the strongest known [[X-ray]] sources) up to the construction of the Z-machine at [[Sandia National Laboratories]] under [[Thomas W. L. Sanford|Tom Sanford]]. In 2006, he and his colleagues proposed a model to explain the record temperatures of 2 to 3 billion kelvins generated in the Z machine—the eddies formed by the numerous [[Plasma stability|instabilities]] of the intense [[magnetic field]] are slowed down in the dense plasma and give their energy to the ions.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Physik|first=Welt der|title=Hitzerekord im Labor - warum es im Plasma so heiß wird und effektiv Röntgenstrahlung abgibt|url=https://www.weltderphysik.de/gebiet/materie/news/2006/hitzerekord-im-labor-warum-es-im-plasma-so-heiss-wird-und-effektiv-roentgenstrahlung-abgibt/|access-date=2020-12-08|website=www.weltderphysik.de|language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Haines|first1=M. G.|last2=LePell|first2=P. D.|last3=Coverdale|first3=C. A.|author3-link=Christine Coverdale|last4=Jones|first4=B.|last5=Deeney|first5=C.|last6=Apruzese|first6=J. P.|date=2006|title=Ion Viscous Heating in a Magnetohydrodynamically Unstable $Z$ Pinch at Over 2×10<sup>9</sup> Kelvin|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=96|issue=7|article-number=075003|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.075003|pmid=16606100}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1995, Haines was inducted as a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name=":1" /> In 2005, he received the [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] with [[Thomas W. L. Sanford|Tom Sanford]] and [[Valentin Panteleimonovich Smirnov|Valentin Smirnov]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lister|first=Jo|date=2005|title=Award of the 2005 Hannes Alfvén Prize of the European Physical Society to Malcolm Haines, Tom Sanford and Valentin Smirnov|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0741-3335/47/12B/E02|journal=Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion|volume=47|issue=12B|doi=10.1088/0741-3335/47/12B/E02|s2cid=250850964 |issn=0741-3335|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
